If the "kick" signal is not received within a given timeout period, the timer should assert a reset signal. The timer should be parameterized to allow for different timeout values.

module WatchdogTimer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset_n,
    input wire kick,
    output reg reset_signal
);
    parameter TIMEOUT = 10; // Timeout value in clock cycles
    reg [3:0] counter; // 4-bit counter to track time

    always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
        if (!reset_n) begin
            counter <= 0;
            reset_signal <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (kick) begin
                counter <= 0; // Reset the counter on kick
                reset_signal <= 1'b0; // De-assert reset_signal
            end else if (counter < TIMEOUT) begin
                counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
                reset_signal <= 1'b0; // De-assert reset_signal
            end else begin
                reset_signal <= 1'b1; // Assert reset_signal if timeout
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire reset,
    input wire send_data,
    input wire receive_data,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: SEND, 10: RECEIVE
);

    parameter SEND = 2'b01;
    parameter RECEIVE = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (send_data) begin
                        state <= SEND;
                    end else if (receive_data) begin
                        state <= RECEIVE;
                    end
                end
                SEND: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Return to IDLE after sending

                    state <= IDLE; // Return to IDLE after receiving

            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

            case ({J, K})

                2'b01: Q <= 0;         // Reset  
                2'b10: Q <= 1;         // Set  
                2'b11: Q <= ~Q;        // Toggle  
            endcase  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg is_empty,
    output reg is_full
);

    reg [2:0] top; // points to the top of the stack

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin

            is_empty <= 1'b1;
            is_full <= 1'b0;

                is_empty <= 1'b0;

                data_out <= stack[top];
                top <= top - 1;
                if (top == 3'b111) is_empty <= 1'b1; // Stack is empty now

        end
    end

    output reg valid_out
);

    reg [3:0] sent_count; // Number of packets sent

        if (rst) begin
            state <= 0;
            sent_count <= 0;
            packet_out <= 0;
            valid_out <= 0;

                        sent_count <= sent_count + 1;

    end

  - `req_b`: Request signal from channel B
  - `ack_a`: Acknowledge signal for channel A
  - `ack_b`: Acknowledge signal for channel B
  - `data_in_a`: Data input from channel A

  - `active_channel`: Indicates which channel is currently active (0 for A, 1 for B)

    input clk,
    input reset,
    input req_a,
    input req_b,
    input ack_a,
    input ack_b,
    input [7:0] data_in_a,
    input [7:0] data_in_b,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg active_channel
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            active_channel <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle state
                    if (req_a) begin
                        active_channel <= 0;
                        data_out <= data_in_a;
                        state <= 1; // Transition to transferring state
                    end else if (req_b) begin
                        active_channel <= 1;
                        data_out <= data_in_b;
                        state <= 1; // Transition to transferring state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // Transferring state
                    if (active_channel == 0 && ack_a) begin
                        state <= 0; // Go back to idle

                        state <= 0; // Go back to idle

1. A sender module that transmits data and waits for an acknowledgment (ACK) from the receiver.

3. The system should be able to retry sending the data if a NACK is received.
4. Implement a simple parity check for the error detection.
5. The sender should have a maximum of 3 retries before giving up.

The sender and receiver should communicate through a simple handshake mechanism.

    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire ack,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg send,
    output reg retry
);
    reg [2:0] state;
    reg [2:0] retry_count;
    parameter IDLE = 3'b000, SEND = 3'b001, WAIT_ACK = 3'b010, RETRY = 3'b011, DONE = 3'b100;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            retry_count <= 0;
            send <= 0;
            retry <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    data_out <= data_in; // Prepare data to send
                    state <= SEND;
                end
                
                SEND: begin
                    send <= 1; // Indicate sending data
                    state <= WAIT_ACK;
                end
                
                WAIT_ACK: begin
                    if (ack) begin
                        send <= 0; // Acknowledged
                        state <= DONE;
                    end else begin
                        if (retry_count < 3) begin
                            retry_count <= retry_count + 1;
                            state <= RETRY;
                        end else begin
                            state <= DONE; // Give up after retries
                        end
                    end
                end
                
                RETRY: begin
                    send <= 1; // Retry sending data
                    state <= WAIT_ACK;
                end
                
                DONE: begin
                    send <= 0;
                    retry <= 0; // Finish operation
                    state <= IDLE; // Reset state to IDLE
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule
